title: Product transitions for a system of pushforwards
statement: Let $J$ be a small category, $F:J\to\mathrm{Cat}$ a functor, and $T_j$ Grothendieck topologies on $F(j)$ such that each $F(a)$ is continuous [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Write $R_a$ for continuous pushforward, $c_{a,b}:R_aR_b\simeq R_{ab}$ and $E_j:R_{1_j}\simeq\mathrm{Id}$ for the canonical comparisons. Given abelian sheaves $M_j,A_j$, maps $\phi_a:M_j\to R_aM_k$ satisfying $\phi_{ab}=\phi_a R_a(\phi_b)c_{a,b}$, and arbitrary maps $i_j:M_j\to A_j$, set $B_j=\prod_{t:j\to k}R_t A_k$, $G_j=A_j\times B_j$, and $\gamma_j=((1-\phi_{1_j}E_j)i_j,(\phi_tR_t(i_k))_t)$. There are maps $\psi_a:G_j\to R_aG_k$ satisfying $\psi_{ab}=\psi_aR_a(\psi_b)c_{a,b}$ and $\phi_aR_a(\gamma_k)=\gamma_j\psi_a$. Neither injectivity of the $A_j$ nor monicity of $i_j$ is assumed or concluded.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0EXZ proof, displayed product and transition formula

proof.text: Write C_ab for the canonical pushforward composition comparison. Define q_a:B_j → R_a B_k by the universal product map whose t-component is π_(a≫t) followed by C_at inverse. Pushforward preserves products, since it is right adjoint to sheaf pullback. Checking the component indexed by t reduces the cocycle for q to F.map_comp and F.map_assoc, hence to naturality and coherence of the comparison.
The maps d_j:M_j → B_j with t-component φ_t R_t(i_k) satisfy φ_a R_a(d_k)=d_j q_a by the assumed cocycle, comparison naturality at i_k, and the product projection equations.
Set e_j=φ_id E_j. The cocycle with the second arrow identity and identity-comparison coherence imply φ_a R_a(e_k)=φ_a. Thus φ_a R_a((1-e_k)i_k)=0 because continuous pushforward is additive.

Define ψ_a on A_j × B_j with zero component toward R_a A_k and q_a after the second projection toward R_a B_k, using the inverse binary-product comparison. Its cocycle follows by checking the two projections: the first is zero, and the second is the cocycle of q. Compatibility of γ follows similarly from the preceding two steps.
